reason: The pen needs a holder and lift mechanism before it can draw from the rover.

choice.with: Spring pen clip with lift lever

expectation: The pen will fit into the clip to make a liftable drawing tool.

effect: The pen is now clipped and ready to fit to the rover.
reaction: That was the expected first assembly.
reason: The clipped pen needs to be mounted on the tested rover.
expectation: The pen assembly will attach to the rover.

effect: The clipped pen is mounted on the rover, so it can be tested on paper.
reason: The test-paper roll provides a surface for checking how the rover draws.
expectation: The rover will make a test drawing, revealing whether the pen needs adjustment.

alternatives.reason: The pen might need adjustment first, but a test could show what adjustment is needed.

effect: The test revealed unequal motor speeds and identified the receiver’s trim as the adjustment to try.
reaction: The curve makes the purpose of the screwdriver clear.
reason: The screwdriver should let me adjust the receiver’s trim to correct the curve.
expectation: Adjusting the trim will bring the wheel speeds closer together so the rover can drive straighter.

effect: The trim has been adjusted and checked with another line; the rover is ready for further remote testing.
reaction: It is useful to see the correction made at the control rather than to the drawing.
reason: The remote should let me test steering and the pen lift on the trimmed rover.
expectation: The rover will draw and steer under remote control, with its pen raised when needed.

effect: The remote test completed the rover: differential wheel speeds steer it, while the clip lever lifts the pen between drawings.
reaction: The looping whale is a satisfying payoff for the earlier test and adjustment.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the rover on paper was most worthwhile: the curve made the unequal motor speeds visible and gave the trim adjustment a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Clipping and mounting the pen were necessary but predictable, with little to discover on their own.

surprise.text: The straight-ahead command produced a curve because one motor was quicker; adjusting the receiver could correct the control.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the screwdriver had an unclear purpose until the drawing test revealed the trim problem.

continue.text: Yes. The test-and-adjust sequence made the mechanism understandable, and drawing a whale was an appealing payoff; I would be curious to see what the fair does with the rover.
